title: Lizard_DT_Assignment_Scoring_v1
description: Scoring output schema for the kertenkele final exam. Takes extraction JSON as input and produces a structured scoring document. Automated criteria are computed by the pipeline from extraction fields. LLM criteria require an LLM pass over the raw_text or code_evidence fields. Human criteria require a reviewer.

rubric_version.description: Rubric point values are subject to instructor revision. Tag this field when points change.

llm_model.description: Model ID used for LLM scoring pass. Null for automated-only runs.

global_flags.description: Pre-scoring checks derived from extraction fields. These govern score eligibility across sections — computed before any criterion is scored.

synthetic_data_used.description: Copied from extraction.data_source.synthetic_data_used. When true, all S4 MCR-table criteria and S5 test_mcr criteria are set to 0 points with flag 'mcr_invalid_synthetic_data'.

infrastructure_interrupt.description: Copied from extraction.execution.infrastructure_interrupt. When true, cells_with_errors in execution is not penalized.

all_three_targets_attempted.description: True if dt_experiments contains entries for all three required targets: YasamAlani, Tur, Cinsiyet.

mcr_tables_complete_count.description: Count of dt_experiments where mcr_table has exactly 10 rows (depth 1–10). Drives S4.1 automated check.

step4_responses_per_tree_count.description: Count of dt_experiments where step4_responses_location == 'per_tree' AND at least one step4_markdown_analysis field is non-null.

step4_responses_aggregated.description: True if any dt_experiment has step4_responses_location == 'aggregated_end_of_notebook'. Scoring note: aggregated responses are distributed equally across all trees they cover.

any_cells_with_errors.description: True if extraction.execution.cells_with_errors > 0 AND infrastructure_interrupt is false.

section_scores.description: One scoring block per rubric section. Section IDs map to assignment steps.

S1.description: Veri Keşfi — Step 1 data exploration questions and code evidence. 10 points.

S1.1.criterion: Dataset loaded and shape confirmed. data_loaded==true AND row_count_reported==320 AND col_count_reported==7.

S1.2.criterion: Habitat distribution answered: most-frequent AND least-frequent habitat named correctly (Yer / Agac).
S1.2.automated_rule: 2 pts if both present and contain 'Yer' and 'Agac' respectively (case-insensitive). 1 pt if one correct. 0 if both null.

S1.3.criterion: Class imbalance effect on the model explained. q_imbalance_effect_reasoning is non-null AND contains a reasoning about model bias or minority-class error.
S1.3.llm_rubric: 3 pts: explains that the majority class (Yer) will be predicted better and the minority (Agac) will have higher error, using model reasoning (not just 'more data = better'). 2 pts: identifies the asymmetry but without model-level reasoning. 1 pt: vague answer ('model will be affected'). 0 pts: null or off-topic.

S1.4.criterion: Mass differences across species explained with biological or data reasoning.
S1.4.llm_rubric: 3 pts: identifies Sceloporus as largest, Uta as smallest, provides a biological or ecological reason. 2 pts: correct species ordering without explanation, or explanation without correct ordering. 1 pt: partial or vague. 0 pts: null.

S2.description: Araştırma Soruları — At least 3 research questions formulated, one per target. 5 points.

S2.1.criterion: Three targets present, each with a non-null formulated_question.
S2.1.automated_rule: 1 pt per non-null formulated_question for a distinct required target (YasamAlani, Tur, Cinsiyet). Max 3 pts.

S2.2.criterion: Question quality: each question is a specific predictive question (not just a restatement of the target variable name).
S2.2.llm_rubric: 2 pts: all present questions are phrased as a classification question ('Bu kertenkelenin ... nedir?' or similar). 1 pt: at least one specific question found. 0 pts: all null or all restate column names only.

S3.description: Train/Test Split — Parameter correctness and conceptual questions. 5 points.

S3.1.criterion: Correct split parameters: test_size=0.2, stratify_used=true, random_state set to any integer.
S3.1.automated_rule: 2 pts if all three correct. 1 pt if test_size and stratify correct but random_state null. 0 pts if stratify=false or test_size wrong.

S3.2.criterion: stratify removal effect explained in terms of class distribution in the test set.
S3.2.llm_rubric: 2 pts: explains that removing stratify could cause unequal class representation in train/test sets, with reference to the minority class (Agac) or imbalance. 1 pt: correct direction but no class-level reasoning. 0 pts: null or 'nothing changes'.

S3.3.criterion: random_state change effect explained: results change but model structure stays the same.
S3.3.llm_rubric: 1 pt: explains that random_state controls which samples go to train/test, so results change slightly but model behavior is not fundamentally different. 0 pts: null or incorrect.

S4.description: Derinlik Analizi — Per-tree depth loop, MCR table, and markdown analysis. 30 points (10 per tree). When synthetic_data_used=true, S4.1 per-tree is 0 pts (flag: mcr_invalid_synthetic_data). When step4_responses_location is null for a tree, S4.2–S4.5 for that tree are 0 pts (flag: step4_missing).

eligible.description: False if synthetic_data_used=true. When false, all criteria in this block are 0 and flag is set.

S4.x.1.criterion: MCR table present and covers depth 1–10 (10 rows).
S4.x.1.automated_rule: 3 pts if mcr_table has exactly 10 rows with depth 1–10. 2 pts if 8–9 rows. 1 pt if < 8 rows but at least 5. 0 pts if null or < 5 rows.

S4.x.2.criterion: Trend accurately described: training MCR decreases monotonically; test MCR has a minimum then rises.
S4.x.2.automated_rule: Verify from mcr_table: is train MCR monotonically non-increasing? Does test MCR have a minimum below depth 10? Set automated_check.result accordingly.
S4.x.2.llm_rubric: 2 pts: student text correctly identifies both directions (train falls, test has minimum). 1 pt: identifies one direction only. 0 pts: null or contradicts the table data.

S4.x.3.criterion: Overfitting correctly named or meaningfully described.
S4.x.3.automated_rule: 1 pt base if overfitting_named_or_described is non-null.
S4.x.3.llm_rubric: 2 pts: uses the word 'overfitting' / 'aşırı öğrenme' AND explains the mechanism (train error falls while test error rises). 1 pt: names it correctly but explanation absent or vague. 0 pts: null.

S4.x.4.criterion: Divergence point between training and test curves identified.
S4.x.4.llm_rubric: 1 pt: specifies a depth or range where the two curves separate. 0 pts: null or says 'they always diverge'.

S4.x.5.criterion: Preferred depth stated with justification from both table and graph.
S4.x.5.llm_rubric: 2 pts: preferred depth cited from table AND graph, both consistent with each other and with the mcr_table minimum. 1 pt: only one source cited, or depth inconsistent with minimum but with stated reasoning. 0 pts: null or depth contradicts both sources without explanation.

S5.description: Final Karar Ağacı — Per-tree final model, depth choice, visualization, and interpretation. 21 points (7 per tree).

S5.x.1.criterion: Model pipeline complete: model_built AND model_fitted AND tree_visualized AND mcr_plot_generated.
S5.x.1.automated_rule: 2 pts if all four are true. 1 pt if model_built+model_fitted true but visualization missing. 0 pts if model not built.

S5.x.2.criterion: Chosen depth is mathematically optimal (minimum test MCR in mcr_table).
S5.x.2.automated_rule: 2 pts if is_optimal_depth_mathematically_correct == true. 1 pt if chosen depth is within 1 of mathematically_optimal_depth. 0 pts otherwise.

S5.x.3.criterion: Root node feature correctly identified and reported (student-reported vs computed agreement).
S5.x.3.automated_rule: 1 pt if root_node_feature (student-reported) matches the base variable name of root_node_feature_computed (e.g. 'Cinsiyet_Erkek' reported as 'Cinsiyet' is acceptable — stem match). 1 pt also if root_node_feature is null and source is 'computed' (student omitted but code ran correctly). 0 pts if student-reported and computed contradict and source is 'markdown_text'.

S5.x.4.criterion: Root node reasoning addresses why that feature is the most discriminative.
S5.x.4.llm_rubric: 1 pt: reasoning mentions the feature's discriminative power or a biological/data-driven explanation for why it splits best. 0 pts: null, circular ('because the model chose it'), or off-topic.

S5.x.5.llm_rubric: 1 pt: references the CODAP tree the student built earlier in the course, notes a similarity or difference in root node or structure. 0 pts: null or does not reference CODAP.

S6.description: Yazılı Yansıma — 4 reflection questions. 20 points (5 per question). Scored by LLM. All raw_text fields must be verbatim from extraction.

S6.1.criterion: Q1 — Öğrenme Yolculuğu: reflective comparison across data cards, CODAP, and Python environments.
S6.1.llm_rubric: 5 pts: discusses all three environments with distinct observations, identifies where understanding was deepest, and addresses error detection. 4 pts: three environments present but one observation is superficial. 3 pts: two environments or error detection missing. 2 pts: one environment only or generic response. 1 pt: raw_text present but no substantive reflection. 0 pts: null.

S6.2.criterion: Q2 — Veri Anlayışı: biological reasoning about root node selection and misclassification patterns.
S6.2.llm_rubric: 5 pts: biological explanation of root feature (why Sceloporus/mass/length is discriminative), addresses surprise or expectation, AND discusses which habitat is hardest to classify with a plausible biological reason. 4 pts: two of three dimensions present. 3 pts: biological reasoning present but shallow on misclassification. 2 pts: correct direction but generic phrasing. 1 pt: raw_text present, no biological reasoning. 0 pts: null.

S6.3.criterion: Q3 — Model Performansı: MCR interpretation, cross-target comparison, and performance threshold reasoning.
S6.3.llm_rubric: 5 pts: states correct MCR value, identifies best and worst predicted class with a reason tied to data properties (morphological overlap, class size), proposes a numeric threshold for 'good' model, and compares performance across targets. 4 pts: three of four dimensions. 3 pts: MCR stated and best/worst class but no cross-target comparison or threshold. 2 pts: MCR stated but reasoning missing. 1 pt: partial text, no MCR value. 0 pts: null.
S6.3.automated_pre_check: Verify mcr_value_stated matches test_mcr_achieved from at least one dt_experiment. If mismatch > 0.01, flag for LLM attention.

S6.4.criterion: Q4 — Karar Ağacının Sınırları: error pattern, data/model improvement, and plain-language explanation.
S6.4.llm_rubric: 5 pts: identifies a systematic error pattern (not random), proposes data-level and/or model-level improvement, names an alternative model with a reason, AND provides a clear lay explanation of decision trees including the overfitting limitation. 4 pts: three of four dimensions. 3 pts: error pattern + explanation only, no alternative or improvement. 2 pts: lay explanation only. 1 pt: partial. 0 pts: null.

S7.description: Çapraz Hedef Karşılaştırma — Explicit comparison across all three trees. 9 points.

S7.1.criterion: Cross-target comparison section present in the notebook.
S7.1.automated_rule: 1 pt if comparison_present == true. 0 pts otherwise.

S7.2.criterion: Optimal depth differences across targets explained (each target may require a different depth).
S7.2.llm_rubric: 4 pts: explains WHY optimal depths differ — e.g. Tur is more separable so fewer levels needed; Cinsiyet is noisier so more depth needed but still overfit early. References the specific MCR values or depth numbers. 3 pts: notes depths differ with a partial reason. 2 pts: notes depths differ, no reason. 1 pt: comparison_present but reasoning absent. 0 pts: null.

S7.3.criterion: Root node differences across targets noted and interpreted.
S7.3.llm_rubric: 4 pts: notes that different targets have different root nodes AND provides a biological or statistical interpretation (e.g. mass/length discriminates species, not gender). 3 pts: notes root node changes with partial reasoning. 2 pts: notes change, no reason. 1 pt: vague mention. 0 pts: null or no root node comparison.

grand_total_possible.description: S1(10)+S2(5)+S3(5)+S4(30)+S5(21)+S6(20)+S7(9)=100. Const 90 set for rubric v1 — pending instructor sign-off on S7 weight.

scoring_overrides.description: Human reviewer corrections applied after automated/LLM scoring. Each override replaces points_awarded for a specific criterion.

score_value.description: Actual awarded points. Null means not yet scored. Must not exceed the criterion's points_possible.

id.description: Criterion ID matching rubric_reference keys, e.g. 'S1.1', 'S4.YasamAlani.3'.

scoring_mode.description: automated = pipeline computes from extraction fields with no LLM. llm = LLM reads raw_text and scores. hybrid = automated base check + LLM text quality adjustment. human = reviewer only.

automated_check.description: Result of the automated pre-check for hybrid/automated criteria.

justification.description: LLM-generated or reviewer-written explanation of the awarded score.

flag.description: Special condition that affected scoring logic for this criterion.
